research.title: Binary number
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "Numbers by position": Planet 1 spells its numbers with three marks in exactly this way.

research.title: Chinese character classification
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "Signs built from meaningful parts": Planet 2's signs are built from parts too, though there every part carries meaning and none carries sound.

research.title: Coding of Nominal Plurality (chapter by Matthew S. Dryer)
research.by: World Atlas of Language Structures Online
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "Saying there is more than one": Planet 3 uses a separate small sign after the noun.

research.title: Negative Morphemes (chapter by Matthew S. Dryer)
research.by: World Atlas of Language Structures Online
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "Saying no": Planet 3's negation is simpler than that: it removes a thing, not a whole statement.

research.title: Linear B
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "Reading a script nobody could read": You are working the same way: patterns and context, with no dictionary to hand.

research.title: Arecibo message
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "A message meant for strangers": Numbers and pictures were chosen because they might survive a trip between minds that share no language.

inspiration.title: Chants of Sennaar
inspiration.note: The idea of learning a language by watching how its glyphs are used and filling in a notebook of guesses, with the game's own invented languages and story.

inspiration.title: The Message from Deep Space
inspiration.note: Named alongside Chants of Sennaar as the kind of deduction puzzle wanted; Lexis keeps its own original premise of a message that has to be understood.

inspiration.title: Star Trek
inspiration.note: The first-contact survey ship premise, a crew opening a conversation on each new planet, is Star Trek-flavoured in spirit with an original ship, crew and worlds.

other.title: Pyodide
other.note: Runs the game's Python rules in the browser through WebAssembly (version 0.26.4, loaded from a CDN), so the game needs no server of its own and no build step.
